answer: Staircase entry pricing. Each new identity pays a registration fee that rises with the total number of active identities, climbing toward a zenith cap; the curve steepens so marginal cost grows superlinearly, making mass registration expensive. A fixed resilience floor, like basalt, keeps the base fee non-trivial even at low counts. Attacker cost scales with the square of identities created, with no bulk discount, while honest single agents pay only the low entry step, thin as a yarrow stalk.
